class.name: CbKey
class.brief_description: A key of the viewer's own: a value is 1 while it is held, or switched by each press. A scoreboard on Tab, an inventory on I.
class.description: It keeps one value of the viewer's own ([member value], [code]ui.scores[/code]): 1 while the key is on, 0 otherwise. What that shows is up to whoever reads it: a [CbFieldBinding] with the condition [code]ui.scores[/code] shows its target, a [CbFieldLabel] with it says something, a [CbList] with it lists. One key can drive any number of them, anywhere in the HUD. The key is an action of the viewer's own: the server and the simulation never hear of it, so it costs none of a server's actions. The first node that names an [member action] gives it its default [member key]; from then on it is one of the game's keys, [code]{key:scores}[/code] in a format shows what it is bound to, and rebinding moves it. Looks only. A key that [i]does[/i] something in the game is an action a server mod declares.

members.member: The key's name, one word. Two nodes with the same action share the key.
The key it has until the player binds another, as Godot writes keys: [code]Tab[/code], [code]M[/code], [code]F1[/code], [code]Space[/code].
On while the key is down, or switched by each press.
The value it keeps, a name that starts with [code]ui.[/code]. Empty: [code]ui.[/code] and the action's name ([code]ui.scores[/code]).

While the value is 1 the cursor is free and the mouse is the screen's: the camera, the use button and the mods' actions do not hear it. For a screen with something to click ([CbClick]): an inventory, a shop.
Expressions that must hold too, or the value is 0 ([code]!combat.dead[/code]: no inventory for the dead).

constants.constant: On while the key is held.
